To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the number of disjoint Lagrangian copies of a given real hypersurface $\mathcal L $ in a complex projective hypersurfaces of large degree grows linearly in the dimension of the homology of the hypersurface.

the number of Lagrangian subspaces of given homology class in a random complex projective hypersurfaces grows linearly with the homology class, and that the probability that a random projective complex curve of given degree has a short systole is positive and uniform in the degree.

the probability of a random complex projective algebraic variety to contain many disjoint Lagrangians of a fixed real hypersurface is positive, provided that the latter has non-vanishing Euler characteristic.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following question: how does a random smooth complex projective variety of large degree behave with respect to its symplectic geometry?
the study of the distribution of Lagrangian sub-manifolds and systoles of random complex algebraically integrable systems.
the geometry and the topology of random complex hypersurfaces.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

for a large power of a given ample line bundle, a large proportion of the corresponding vanishing loci are equipped with many Lagrangian subspaces diffeomorphic to a given compact smooth affine hypersurface.

for any compact smooth real affine hypersurface $\mathcal L\subset\mathbb{R}$, there is a positive probability that a random complex projective hypersurfaces of large degree contains many disjoint Lagrangian copies of $\mathcal{L}$, provided that the connected components of the latter hypersurface have non vanishing homology, which implies that the dimension of the ambient space is odd.
the probability of having small systoles for a random projective complex algebraic variety with respect to an ample metric is positive.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
random algebraic geometry can help to understand the geometry of Lagrangian subvarieties.
the geometry of a large class of random complex hypersurfaces is very similar to that of their real counterparts.
we prove a probabilistic version of a theorem of Gromov and Lawson on the existence of closed Lagrangian sub-manifolds of projective complex manifolds.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the topology of random complex hypersurfaces is very similar to the one of real algebraic hypersurfa ces, and that the latter can be studied using the same probabilistic tools as the former.
, under suitable assumptions, the topology of a random complex algebraic variety is very likely to be rich.
the topology of the vanishing loci is strongly related to that of the ambient manifold.
